brique._comment: Engine-native Matter family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: matter.derive
objective.description: Create one new derived matter in the local context from caller-supplied descriptor content and lineage.

#root.role: Build a new derived matter descriptor, preserve caller-supplied lineage, optionally seed brique-managed substance, and register the new matter in the local catalog.

target_matter_id._comment: Optional. Name for the derived matter within the current context. Auto-generated by the engine when absent.

matter._comment: Optional opaque derived matter descriptor seed. The four canonical object sections (brique, objective, subjective, functional) are ensured by the engine when absent so the descriptor remains eligible for meaning projection.

derived_from._comment: Optional. Lineage value stored as-is in the matter descriptor under the 'derived_from' key. Accepts any JSON value: a string, an array of strings (e.g. source matter IDs), an object, or any other JSON-serializable value. The engine does not interpret or validate its shape.

payload._comment: Optional initial substance. Allowed only when the resulting derived matter uses brique substance mode.

derived_target._comment: The concrete derived matter is the target designated or generated for params.target_matter_id in the current context.

effects.matter_descriptor: A new derived matter descriptor is written.
effects.matter_substance: A brique-managed data.bin may be created when the selected substance mode allows payload materialization.
effects.catalog: The local matter catalog gains the derived matter.

transformation_contract.morphing: A caller-supplied derived matter definition and lineage becomes a new committed local matter with explicit lineage carried in its descriptor and local catalog presence.
invariants: If target_matter_id is omitted, the capacity generates a fresh local matter identifier.
The provided derived_from value is stored opaquely and not normalized by the engine.
Payload materialization follows the same brique-mode-only rule as matter.create.
success: On success, matter.derive returns ok=true, the concrete matter_id of the derived target, and the committed revision.
Successful derivation writes matter.json, preserves the caller-supplied lineage field, and updates the local catalog.
failure: The capacity refuses derivation when the designated or generated target matter_id already exists in the runtime catalog.
The capacity fails when the matter descriptor or payload cannot be marshaled or committed to disk.
The capacity refuses payload writes when the supplied matter metadata resolves to a non-brique substance mode.
notes: Derivation creates a new local matter rather than mutating an existing one.
The engine does not interpret lineage semantics beyond storing the supplied derived_from value.
